caption: The drawing consists of a rectangular textile pattern in two colors: dark blue as the background and an off-white or light beige for the woven design. The main section features symmetrical floral and star motifs arranged around a central medallion, with recurring stylized flowers, leaves, and small eight-pointed stars radiating outward. In the lower left, there is a block containing text, four-part: at the top left "1842" is woven, below which a horse and rider face left over the phrase "UNITED WE STAND DIVIDED WE FALL." In the lower border, the words "WASHINGTON", "J. CUNNINGHAM," "WEAVER, NHARTFORD", "ONEIDA CO. NEW YORK", and "BETSY OLDFARMER" appear in capital letters. A row of eagles with outstretched wings and shields on their chests appears above this text, as well as two female figures holding objects. The phrase "UNDER THIS WE PROSPER" repeats above the lower border. In the lower right of the image, separated on the page, is a small inset showing a detail of the textile, including an animal (possibly a deer) and a stylized border. The name "BYRON A. DINGMAN, ALLISON PARK PA" is printed below the textile on the background. The composition is geometric and symmetrical, with an emphasis on repeating borders and balanced imagery. The textile is created in a traditional American coverlet style.
title: Textile of George Washington
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
